timeline.title: The MuSiK Box begins
timeline.copy: Seamus Kelleher and Myles Snider launch the music blog in Cleveland.

timeline.title: In Audio We Trust
timeline.copy: The site adopts a new name as its readership and contributor group grow.

timeline.title: Last recovered entries
timeline.copy: The surviving catalog ends in January 2012 when Seamus and Myles sold the site domains and associated assets.

recoveryNote: A partial recovery, August 2009–January 2012. Original snapshots remain linked throughout.
intro: The MuSiK Box was founded in Cleveland by high school classmates Seamus Kelleher and Myles Snider and became In Audio We Trust in 2011. This archive brings together {{recordCount}} surviving post records, recovered artwork, interviews, and the history of the site which rose in significance, traffic and value from 2009 until its eventual sale in 2012.

picks.title: Artist of the Week

image.alt: J. Cole — Artist of the Week, December 2009

picks.caption: Recovered photo · December 2009
picks.description: The MuSiK Box was among the first blogs to publish J. Cole’s music in 2009. Its November 2009 Artist of the Week feature appeared nearly two years before his debut album, Cole World: The Sideline Story, arrived in September 2011.

picks.title: Early music and interviews
picks.caption: Recovered photo · November 2009. Linked post · Bad Day, October 2010.
picks.description: The MuSiK Box was widely credited with discovering Chiddy Bang while they were still Drexel students with only a MySpace account. The blog interviewed the duo and published their earliest work. In the months that followed, dozens of publications linked back to and credited The MuSiK Box as Chiddy Bang rose to prominence, bringing substantial attention to the blog.

picks.title: His first out-of-town show

image.alt: Mac Miller on The Arroyo Show in 2011, recalling his first out-of-town headlining show at The Grog Shop

picks.description: The MuSiK Box booked his first out-of-town headlining show at The Grog Shop in Cleveland Heights. The August 21, 2010 show took place eight days after the release of his breakthrough mixtape K.I.D.S. and nearly 15 months before his debut album, Blue Slide Park, arrived in November 2011.
picks.caption: Interview still · The Arroyo Show, October 2011
